view: This print is a guided trough quarter, and the bar for it is fresh and low. The one sell-side analyst cut Sep-quarter EPS to -0.13 in the past week, with revenue at $6.44M, about 27% below the $8.8M record June quarter. The company has already told the market the bad part: the satellite pause, losses returning, a further cut in December. On 2026-11-05 it also published the good part: a $2M follow-on from the satellite customer, shipping from December over 2-3 months, which it called 'sooner than expected' and said 'supports forecasted fiscal 2027 results'. That wording points to the guide being reaffirmed, not raised. The stock has already taken that order in, running about 17% to 5.23 before giving back 5.5% today. So the line it trades on, the FY27 guide and the timing of the satellite recovery, is mostly public. The quarter's revenue against a just-lowered single estimate is a small edge for a beat, but I cannot rebuild the quarter well enough to say which side of $6.44M it lands on. The '40%' cut may refer to the satellite program (which would put total revenue near $7-7.8M) or to total revenue (near $5.3M), and the analyst sits between the two. Against that, a 17% run-up into a quarter with a widening loss and lower margin makes a disappointment move more than a beat. On a $100k-a-day tape, the opening print can be several percent off on a few hundred shares. Net: a coin flip with a slight upward tilt, and a typical move of about 6%.

recommendation.reason: The deciding line, the FY27 guide and when the satellite customer recovers, was mostly published on 2026-11-05 and taken in by a 17% run-up. The single estimate was cut in the past week, so the bar is fresh rather than stale, and I cannot place the quarter's revenue on either side of it from public parts. No mechanism clears the 65% bar.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A raised or narrowed-up FY27 revenue guide, or a statement that satellite volumes return to the prior run rate before the March quarter, would make this a clear up. A cut to the $30M low end, or Sep-quarter revenue well under $6M with gross margin under 15%, would make it a clear down.

self_critique: The case for up: the lone analyst, who is the company's underwriter and has management access, just cut the quarter, so a beat against $6.44M is the likelier headline. Management also has a dated, earlier-than-expected order to talk up on the call, and could tighten the guide toward the top. The case for down: the stock ran 17% into a quarter where revenue falls about 27% sequentially, margins compress and losses return. December is guided lower still, and microcap holders often sell an ugly-looking income statement whatever the estimate. Neither case is strong enough to move me past about 52.
